headline: Man jailed for a year over punch that killed a Swede in Copenhagen
headline_short: Fatal punch earns a year in prison
deck: He has earlier convictions for attempted murder and rape; the government will raise the penalty when simple violence kills.
extended: Copenhagen City Court on Wednesday sentenced a 31-year-old man to a year in prison for a punch that killed Christian Zedig, a 32-year-old Swede. The man had pleaded guilty, and he is also barred from nightlife for a year.

On 30 June, at a big-screen showing of a World Cup match at Islands Brygge in Copenhagen, he threw two beer cans at a group that included Zedig. Then he punched him on the head or neck. The blow ruptured an artery. Zedig, who worked for the Swedish police, died on 3 July.

He was convicted of simple rather than aggravated violence. A punch is typically not dangerous, Søren Harbo, a special prosecutor with Copenhagen Police, told the court. The judge counted the man's aggressive behaviour and his earlier convictions, for attempted murder, rape and violence, against him.
Nicolai Wammen, the justice minister, says the government will raise the penalty when simple violence kills. In some such cases, he says, the sentence is 'unacceptably low'.
